items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee addresses the interviewer as 'Bill' ('I’ll be honest with you, Bill') and mentions 'Bill tune' referring to a composition by Miles Davis. No personal relationship with a specific person named 'Bill' other than the interviewer is described.

ctx.x: Why did Miles play the organ? That was the only period that he was doing that?

The first gig at the Fillmore, it was Cedric Lawson on organ. By February he was gone, March he was gone. Lonnie Liston Smith. By April he was gone. Next thing I know, “I’m playing it myself.” Next thing I know, his elbow is on the keyboard. I don’t know. I dared once to go over and play a chord, like this. I could play more piano than he could, because in fact he had me playing for him. We were in Japan. One night we went out afterwards. In Japan, you’re done at 9 o’clock. You play at 6:30. He went out…
In the meantime, you had been working on your own thing. You had this thing with Moses called Open Sky.
